The ownership test is `pg_has_role(current_user, tableowner, 'USAGE')` over `pg_catalog.pg_tables`, which is true for the owner and for any member of the owning role (how a platform's login user maps onto its stable role). `pg_tables` rather than `information_schema` because ownership is the question and the privilege-filtered view (ADR-180) hides exactly the tables a role has no privilege on.
- **Why:** Seen in a live deploy. The admin built the schema (so owns all 42 tables), `DB_INIT` granted the app role read/write and verified it, and the app's own boot then re-applied `schema.sql` and died: `error[42501]: must be owner of table facilitator_account`. The snapshot ends in `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, PostgreSQL requires ownership for *any* ALTER including a no-op one, and the app role did hold CREATE on the schema, so ADR-178's check let it through. Combining ADR-252's two-credential design with a role that has CREATE is exactly this case, and it is the one the design is for.
- **Price:** same as ADR-178. A COLUMN added by a later snapshot is not caught on this path, since the self-repairing ALTERs cannot run. A schema change therefore needs `DB_INIT` with the admin credential (or `./db-provision.sh`), not just a redeploy; the boot log says `provisioned by another role`.
- **Impact:** `db/bootstrap.ts`, the `verified` log lines in `index.ts` and `setup-cli.ts`.

**Validation.** `bootstrap.test.ts` adds 3 tests on a real PGlite role: an admin-built database seen by a CREATE-holding app role returns `verified` instead of throwing; the same role against a partly-built database refuses and names `DATABASE_URL_ADMIN`; and a role that owns its tables still applies the snapshot and reports `unchanged`. **Bite check, watched to fail:** with the ownership guard disabled, the first test fails with `must be owner of table facilitator…` — the deploy's own error — and the second with `permission denied for table cluster`. **Not run:** against the provider's database; the claim that a platform login maps to a role that owns or inherits the tables is the part this cannot test, and is why `pg_has_role` rather than a name comparison.

### ADR-256 — the Sentosa backdrop renders at every width; the 760px handset gate is removed

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** ADR-022 (the backdrop and its box), ADR-193/200 (the photoreal variant and its smoothing), ADR-098 (the shell is the viewport), `apps/web/src/components/participant/BeachScene.test.tsx`
- **Decision:** `.gb-scene` and every rule that styles or animates it are unconditional. The box keeps its desktop geometry verbatim — `position: fixed`, full width, `height: 56.25vw` (16:9), bottom-pinned, `z-index: -1` — at handset widths too. The shell background is the flat `--scene-sky` at every width (the blue-to-yellow gradient it replaces is deleted), and the `prefers-reduced-motion` scene rules lose their width condition along with the rest. No cover-crop, no portrait re-composition, no second geometry.
  - **Why:** Reported from a phone on Android Chrome: "a blue and yellow blank backdrop; there isn't the Sentosa scenery that shows up on desktop." Assessment found no Android rendering failure. `.gb-scene` was `display: none` by default and every scene rule lived inside `@media (min-width: 760px)`, so at a phone's 360–430px viewport the scene never rendered on *any* mobile browser; what the report describes is the shell's fallback gradient (`--sky` → `--sea` → `--sand`) showing through exactly as styled. The gate was deliberate (ADR-022-era rationale, preserved in the pre-fix comment): on a handset the panels cover it anyway, and a half-hidden Merlion reads as a glitch. That mistook "partly covered" for "invisible" — the column's margins, panel gaps and the strip above the nav are where the room shows — and it priced the backdrop at zero for the device class participants actually hold. Cost of showing it: the drawn scene is 73 KB of PNG in total.
  - **Rejected:** (a) `background-size: cover`-style filling of a portrait screen, which crops the 480×270 panorama horizontally and cuts the Merlion off one side and the court off the other — the original glitch, recreated deliberately; (b) a portrait-specific taller box (`background-size: 100% 100%` already stretches the panorama to the box, and non-16:9 heights unglue every percentage anchor the layers are positioned by); (c) blaming `image-rendering: pixelated`, `background-attachment: fixed` or Android's fixed-position compositing — none is in the scene's render path below 760px because the scene was not in the render path at all. Fixing the gate is the whole diagnosis; each alternative treats a symptom the code never had.
- **Impact:** `apps/web/src/styles/gameboy.css` only, plus the one stylesheet test in `BeachScene.test.tsx` that pinned "off handsets" as correct and now pins the opposite. Desktop rendering is byte-identical in effect: the hoisted rules are the media block's rules with the wrapper removed. The `?backdrop=real` variant inherits the change — it remains opt-in by URL, and its 16 MB is still only fetched when a participant's stored choice asks for it. On a handset the scene now animates (drift, cable cars, players) exactly as on desktop; reduced-motion stops it at every width.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: the BeachScene stylesheet assertions re-pinned to "no width gate, displayed and fixed, reduced-motion unconditional" and watched against the old CSS (the negated `@media (min-width: 760px)` assertion and the `.gb-scene { display: block; position: fixed;` assertion both fail on the pre-fix file, for the reason the phone reported). Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh` (typecheck, lint, standards, web build, full web + API suites) — Playwright was **not run** and no browser is available in the sandbox (the Chromium download is outside its allowlist, per `AGENTS-workflow.md` §4), and jsdom applies no media queries in any case — so the unit test proves the text of the stylesheet, not a rendered pixel. The honest Android proof is still a phone: reload a participant surface on the reporting device and the panorama with its moving layers should sit behind the column. This ADR does not claim that check has happened.

### ADR-257 — the staff console is light and high-contrast by default; dark is a stored toggle

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** ADR-019 (`localStore` owns every key), ADR-047 (the photo wall), `apps/web/src/lib/hooks/useConsoleTheme.ts`, `apps/web/src/styles/console.css.test.ts`
- **Decision:** The facilitator and superadmin surfaces default to a light palette whose text tokens clear WCAG AA (4.5:1) on their grounds, asserted numerically in `console.css.test.ts` rather than eyeballed. A Dark/Light toggle in the console bar (and on the two sign-in pages, which render outside the shell) flips it; the choice persists per device in `psd.console-theme.v1`, read only by `useConsoleTheme.ts`. The mechanism is a `data-console-theme` attribute scoping CSS custom-property overrides — no layout, type scale or tap-target change. Anything unreadable in the store means light.
- **Why:** Requested from the field: staff screens are used outdoors on beaches, in glare, all day, and a dark UI loses that fight. Dark stays one tap away for the evening desk rather than being taken away. The photo wall and scanner stay black regardless — their darkness is functional (photographs and a camera feed), so the wall renders without the attribute and its caption colour is pinned explicitly rather than inherited.
- **Price:** The palette now exists twice, and the contrast test is the only thing keeping the pair honest; a component that hard-codes a dark fill instead of using a token will look wrong in light mode until somebody notices. The toggle button itself is unthemed (it renders on either palette).
- **Impact:** `console.css` (light token overrides and fills), `useConsoleTheme.ts`, `ConsoleThemeToggle.tsx`, `ConsoleShell.tsx`, both sign-in pages. The participant (gameboy) surfaces are untouched.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: `console.css.test.ts` parses the light and dark tokens out of the stylesheets and computes their contrast ratios (light text 17.3:1 on panel, muted 7.7:1, accent 6.4:1; no assertion was watched to fail first because the palette was written to pass — the test guards regressions, not the debut); `useConsoleTheme.test.ts` pins light-by-default, stored-dark, garbage-means-light, and persistence; `ConsoleThemeToggle.test.tsx` pins the label naming its destination. Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`. Not run: Playwright (no browser in the sandbox); the rendered check is a facilitator opening the console in daylight.

### ADR-258 — per-row actions live in a kebab (⋮) beside the cluster pill; the big buttons are gone

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** ADR-027 (dangerous acts ask first), ADR-155 (captain-only chat hide), ADR-202 (spoken lines carry faces), `apps/web/src/components/participant/KebabMenu.tsx`
- **Decision:** The team roster's Make captain / Remove and team chat's Hide move from full-width buttons under every row into a small ⋮ overflow menu (`KebabMenu`) placed immediately to the right of the member's or message's cluster/title pill. A kebab, not a hamburger: ☰ denotes an app's navigation drawer, ⋮ denotes "more actions on this thing", and these are actions on one named person or line. The menu owns only view state — open, close on select (before the action runs, so no confirmation ever opens over an open menu), Escape, outside tap — and renders nothing when a row offers no actions. What is behind each item is unchanged, confirmations included (ADR-027, ADR-155), and so are the `data-testid`s the tests drive.
- **Why:** Requested from the field: two big buttons under every teammate dominated a phone screen to serve actions a captain takes rarely, and a Hide button under every chat line did the same. The kebab keeps the affordance on the row it acts on — right of the pill that names its cluster — while the rows themselves become one line each. On the roster the cluster code first became a pill (`gb-badge`) so "right of the pill" is a place that exists.
- **Price:** Actions are one tap further away, and a captain's powers are no longer visible at a glance — the trade the request asked for. Discoverability rests on the ⋮ being a known glyph; the toggle carries an `aria-label` naming the person or author it acts on.
- **Impact:** `KebabMenu.tsx` (+ `.gb-kebab*` in `gameboy.css`), the roster row in `MyTeamPage.tsx`, the message header in `TeamChatPanel.tsx`. The global chat has no per-message moderation to move and is untouched. The staff consoles were considered and left alone: their action buttons sit in desk workflows, not beside cluster pills.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: `KebabMenu.test.tsx` pins nothing-without-options, open/close-before-run, Escape and outside-tap dismissal; the roster and team-chat suites were re-pointed to open the menu before choosing (their confirmations, sends and refusals are asserted exactly as before). Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`. Not run: Playwright (no browser in the sandbox); the rendered check is opening My Team and a team chat on a phone.

### ADR-259 — the kebab's placement is refined: the roster cluster is text again, and the chat kebab sits by the message, not the pill

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** refines ADR-258 (the kebab itself, its ownership of view state, and the rules behind its items are unchanged); ADR-155; `KebabMenu.tsx`
- **Decision:** Two placements ADR-258 got wrong, corrected from the field. (1) The roster's cluster is plain muted text immediately right of the nickname again, exactly as it rendered before ADR-258 — promoting it to a `gb-badge` pill only so the kebab could sit beside it changed a label into chrome. The kebab keeps the roster row's right edge instead. (2) In team chat the kebab leaves the header: the title pill sits alone beside the author, and the kebab moves one line down to the far right of the message body line, top-aligned so a long message keeps it by its first line.
- **Why:** Both complaints are the same one: the affordance was upstaging the content it serves. A pill says "this is a category you can act on"; a cluster code beside a name is just a fact about the person, and dressing it as a badge made every roster row heavier. Likewise the chat kebab belongs to the *message*, so it sits with the words it can hide, not with the title pill in the header.
- **Price:** The kebab is no longer in one identical spot on both screens ("right of the pill"), so the learnability ADR-258 claimed is now "at the right edge of the thing it acts on" — a slightly looser rule, and the one both screens actually satisfy.
- **Impact:** `MyTeamPage.tsx` roster row, `TeamChatPanel.tsx` message row, comments in `KebabMenu.tsx`. Options, confirmations, testids and rules behind the items are untouched.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: the roster suite asserts the cluster beside Alex's nickname is `.gb-hint` text (found via the nickname's own span, since the avatar peek also prints the code); the team-chat suite asserts the header row contains no kebab and the toggle follows the message body in the row. All pre-existing kebab flows (open menu → choose → confirmation → send/refusal) pass unchanged. Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`. Not run: Playwright (no browser in the sandbox); the rendered check is My Team and a team chat on a phone.

### ADR-260 — the passport leads: the profile sends participants to it, its tab comes first, and global chat keeps no kebab

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** ADR-239 (the passport tab), ADR-258/259 (the kebab and where it sits)
- **Decision:** Three navigation facts change together, because they are one idea — the passport is the collection a participant is *pursuing*, and the scan list is the record of how it is going. (1) The profile's Points section button reads **"See my passport"** and links to `/me/scans/passport` (testid `profile__passport-link`, replacing `profile__scans`). (2) The Scan History subtabs swap: **Passport first, Scans second**; routes and active-tab rules (`end` on Scans) are unchanged. (3) Global chat deliberately gains **no kebab**: a participant holds no per-message action in that room, and hiding there is a superadmin act that exists only as an API endpoint. "Consistent with team chat" is satisfied by the shared message layout — author and pill in the header, message, timestamp — and by `KebabMenu`'s existing rule that a row with no options renders no button.
- **Why:** The owner asked for the first two directly, and for the third as a consistency check; on inspection there was nothing in global chat to move. Putting an empty or decorative ⋮ on every global message would teach participants to expect actions that do not exist.
- **Price:** Anything that indexed the tabs by position follows the swap (the unit test and `e2e/participant/passport-stamps.spec.ts` now take the *first* tab for the passport). The button's rename breaks any external note that called it scan history; the scans list is one tap further from the profile than it was, which is the trade the passport-first order intends.
- **Impact:** `ProfilePage.tsx`, `ScanHistoryTabs.tsx`, `participant-pages.test.tsx`, `e2e/participant/passport-stamps.spec.ts`. No route, API or server change.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: the profile test now asserts the button's text, testid and `/me/scans/passport` href; the tab test asserts the swapped href order; the Playwright path takes `nth(0)` for the passport tab. Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`. Not run: Playwright (no browser in the sandbox); the rendered check is the profile button and the subtab row on a phone.

### ADR-261 — repeat rounds strike repeat chops: one impression per counted scan, stacked on the station's slot

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** extends ADR-239 (the tab) and ADR-240/241/242 (the device seed, the generator, the station's die); `apps/api/src/db/entities/scans.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/passport/chopSeeds.ts`, `PassportPage.tsx`
- **Decision:** A station no longer collapses its rounds into one chop. `PassportStationView` gains `completions` — the participant's counted scans at that station, counted exactly as completion already was (ADR-176: voided and undone scans do not count, so a void takes a strike back). The passport renders one impression per completion, stacked over the station's slot in first-strike-first order, each impression fanned slightly over the last and blended multiply like ink over ink. The die is still the station's (ADR-242); the first strike still uses the device's kept seed untouched (ADR-240), so every chop already showing keeps its face; strike N (N ≥ 2) is seeded from that same kept number by the mulberry stream in `chopRandom.ts` (strike N takes its Nth whole-number output), so every strike of the same die differs and none needs storing. In a stack only the first impression is announced to assistive technology — three "Completed"s are one fact.
- **Why:** Requested from the field: a participant who plays the same fringe game in three rounds has *been stamped three times*, and a real passport shows exactly that — the same office's mark struck again, never quite alike. Rejected: (a) storing a fresh random seed per strike on the device, which grows `psd.passportChops.v1` into a list and loses strikes if storage is refused, when derivation from the one kept number reproduces them forever; (b) deriving the repeat seeds from the station id, which ADR-242's rejected option (b) already rules out — every device would strike identical repeats; (c) a count badge ("×3") instead of strikes, which answers with arithmetic what the page exists to show as ink.
- **Price:** A deep stack is heavier to draw — every impression carries two turbulence filters, so a station struck many times costs several filtered SVGs in one row; on the round counts a fringe day actually runs (a handful per station) this is fine, and it is the first place to look if the passport ever scrolls badly. Changing the derivation (or the draw order in `buildChop`) redraws repeat strikes, as with any recipe change (ADR-241). A passport cached by an older build has no `completions`; the hook reads a completed station as one strike until the refresh lands.
- **Impact:** `packages/contracts` (`PassportStationView.completions`), `scans.ts` (grouped count replacing the distinct-id list), `views/passport.ts`, `routes-participants`, `usePassport.ts` (`chop` → `chops`), `chopSeeds.ts` (`chopSeedsFor`), `PassportChop.tsx` (a decorative mode), `PassportPage.tsx` (the stack), `.gb-passport__chops` in `gameboy.css`. Progress ("2 of 5 stations") is unchanged: a station still counts once toward the day.

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: `passport-stations.test.ts` gains counted-scan proof against the real database (three rounds → `completions: 3` and still one completed station; void the third → 2). `chopSeeds.test.ts` pins first-equals-kept, all-distinct, same stack every visit, and unchanged stored shape; `usePassport.test.ts` pins one spec per completion, one die, three distinct placements, first strike identical to the pre-ADR-261 build; `participant-pages.test.tsx` pins three marks stacked on one row (first announced, repeats `aria-hidden`) beside an untouched open slot. The Playwright journey now stamps a second round and expects two differently-placed marks — written, re-pointed where the stack changed its locators, and **not run**: no browser is available in the sandbox. Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`.

### ADR-262 — the stack is capped at three strikes, and each strike must turn and press differently from the one beneath it

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Relates to:** refines ADR-261 (one impression per counted scan); `apps/web/src/lib/passport/chopStack.ts`, `PassportPage.tsx`
- **Decision:** Two refinements to the repeat-strike stack. (1) **Cap:** a station's row draws at most three impressions (`CHOP_STACK_MAX = 3`); the true count stays on the row, and the page folds whatever the cap left undrawn into a gold **"+N more"** pill pinned to the stack's lower-right corner — five completions render three strikes and "+2 more". The hook stops building specs past the cap, so the fold is also the whole rendering cost. (2) **Guaranteed variance:** ADR-261 let each strike's seed fall where it fell, which made lookalike neighbours unlikely but possible. Stack building now enforces what the eye actually compares: every strike after the first must sit at least **3° of rotation** and **0.06 of pressure floor** away from the strike beneath it, redrawing from the next salted derivation stream (attempt 0 is ADR-261's derivation, so stacks that already differ keep their faces) until it clears both, up to 24 attempts. The first strike is never redrawn and still uses the device's kept seed untouched.
- **Why:** Requested from the field on both counts. The cap keeps a much-loved station from becoming a filtered-SVG swamp down the page — every impression carries two turbulence filters, and ADR-261 named exactly this as the first place trouble would show. The fold counts the undrawn strikes rather than pretending they are not there. The variance guarantee is the difference between "generated, so probably different" and what was asked for: stamps that visibly vary in pressure and rotation between strikes, as a hand pressing the same die again actually produces.
- **Price:** A participant cannot inspect strikes four and deeper — there is no expansion gesture behind "+N more", deliberately: the passport shows recent ink, not an archive. Stack building does a little wasted work when a redraw is needed (bounded, deterministic, and identical on every visit and device holding the same seed).
- **Impact:** new `chopStack.ts` (+ tests) owning stack building for `usePassport.ts`; `chopSeeds.ts` exports its derivation with a salted-attempt parameter; `PassportRow` gains the true `completions` beside the capped `chops`; `PassportPage.tsx` renders the fold; `.gb-passport__more` in `gameboy.css`. Server untouched — `completions` already crosses the wire (ADR-261).

**Validation.** Recorded with the change: `chopStack.test.ts` pins the cap (9 completions → 3 specs, 0 → none), first-strike identity with the pre-ADR-261 build, the rotation/pressure minimums pairwise across four stations, and stack stability across visits; `usePassport.test.ts` pins 5 completions → 3 chops with `completions: 5` intact; `participant-pages.test.tsx` pins five completions rendering three marks and a "+2 more" pill. The Playwright journey (two strikes, below the cap) is unchanged in expectation. Full gate per `AGENTS-workflow.md` — `./verify.sh`. Not run: Playwright (no browser in the sandbox); the rendered check is a thrice-played station on a phone.


### ADR-270 — the old tournament is removed whole, ahead of a modular rebuild

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** fds.md §2.5 #obj-court, §2.6 #obj-tournamentmatch, §2.12 #obj-pointconfig, §3.2 #state-match, S21–S24, S41–S49, S60, F22–F25, F37–F38, F42–F44; ADR-089 through ADR-247 (the scheduling, stage and correction work this retires), ADR-1xx/1yy (the shelved manual and drawn days), `docs/design/2026-10-15-tournament-overhaul-plan.md`
- **Decision:** Every piece of the old tournament backend, its superadmin surfaces and its schema is deleted in one change, before the replacement is built. Gone: the `court`, `tournament`, `tournament_plan`, `tournament_entry`, `tournament_fixture`, `tournament_stage`, `tournament_match` and six `manual_*` tables; `point_config`'s tournament columns (win/loss/draw/champion rates, `match_minutes`, `gap_minutes`); `award_batch.stage_id` and `team_award.stage_id`; `'tournamentmatch'` as a void-audit target; every `/api/tournament/*`, `/api/admin/tournament*`, `/api/admin/court-queue`, `/api/admin/courts*`, `/api/admin/matches*` route and `GET /api/teams/:teamId/matches`; the engine, projection and late-entry libraries; the superadmin Tournament, Courts, Court queue and Matches pages. **Teams are not tournament code and stay whole.** The participant, hall-screen and facilitator frontends stay byte-for-byte as they were, still calling the removed paths, until the rebuild serves those paths again in the same wire shapes.
- **Why:** The owner asked for a complete overhaul into a modular engine driven by a switchable scheduler, with the old system cleared first so the new one is not built around its seams. Removing it whole is the only way to find every coupling honestly: the leaderboard, roster repair, the cluster freeze, the dashboard, the operations panel, the export and the alerts all read tournament tables directly, and a partial removal would have left them reading tables that no longer meant what they said. Rejected: building the new engine beside the old one and switching over (the ADR-1xx path) — it already produced two unmounted tournaments in this repository and a third would have tripled the surface the rebuild has to reconcile with.
- **Impact — what reads differently until the rebuild:**
  - The leaderboard's tournament column is award batches only (`leaderboard.ts`); there are no match results or champion bonus to count.
  - The cluster freeze (`hasScoringStarted`) counts fringe scans only.
  - The dashboard reports `courtCount`, `enabledCourtCount` and `matchCount` as 0, and no longer lists B4/B5 blockers; the operations overview reports no live matches, none completed and no teams outside; final standings are provisional with no team tables or podium; `teamUpSoon` is always "not up soon" and the up-soon watcher is gone. Every one of these keeps its wire shape, so the rebuild fills values rather than changing contracts.
  - Roster repair returns `withdrawal: null` and `liveMatchCourtName: null`; disbanding a team no longer touches fixtures, because there are none. `rosterSnapshot` moved to `db/entities/teams.ts` and `RosterSnapshotEntry` to `db/schema/awards.ts`.
  - A facilitator whose default station is a court gets no station label, and the account form offers no courts.
  - The participant Results and Line-ups tabs, team match history, the court console and the hall screen's tournament scenes get 404s from the paths they still call. This is the deliberate interim the owner chose; the rebuild (ADR-272 onward) restores them.
  - The FDS sections above are not edited: this ADR is the divergence, and the rebuild's ADRs record how each surface returns.
  - Stress harness: the court-marshal persona and the feed reads are gone; their weight went to the board.
  - The demo seed no longer creates courts or sets tournament rates; `seed-demo.sql` was regenerated (`./refresh-demo-seed.sh --skip-record`), and `demo-export-cli.ts` now classifies `schema_state` as never exported — the export had refused to run since ADR-264 because the stamp table was unclassified.
  - Playwright: `e2e/exclusive/knockout-pairing.spec.ts` and `e2e/full-event/full-event.spec.ts` are removed; the full-event suite is rebuilt on the new engine.

**Validation.** Typecheck (contracts, api, web), lint and `npm run standards` run on this change; the kept-frontend diff against `2bf76f4` is empty. The regression suites were not required green mid-sprint by the owner's direction — the commit message names exactly which layers ran.

### ADR-271 — a database stamped older than the build is refused at boot, never re-stamped

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-264 (the stamp and `DB_INIT_RESET=stale`), ADR-049 (one snapshot, applied every boot), ADR-270 (the first non-additive change since the stamp existed)
- **Decision:** `ensureSchema` reads the stamp before applying the snapshot. A database that already holds snapshot tables and is stamped **older** than `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (an unstamped one reads 0) makes the boot refuse, naming the remedies: `DB_INIT_RESET=stale` beside `DB_INIT`, `./db-reset.sh`, or `./dev-reset.sh` locally. An empty database still provisions; a current one proceeds; a newer one keeps ADR-264's refusal. `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is now **2**. `resetSchema` drops a `RETIRED_TABLES` list as well as the tables the current file defines.
- **Why:** ADR-264 left a hole that only the first non-additive change could expose: `ensureSchema` stamps whatever it applies, so an old database booted by a newer build was quietly stamped current — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skipped every table it already had, the change the bump recorded never arrived, and the signal `DB_INIT_RESET=stale` reads was erased by the very boot that should have tripped it. And because a reset parsed only the *current* file, a stale database would have kept the retired tournament tables, with their foreign keys into `team` and `facilitator_account`, standing beside the new schema. Rejected: dropping the retired tables automatically on boot — that is a migration, which ADR-049 deliberately does not have, and doing it silently would hide a deployment pointed at the wrong database.
- **Impact:** Every existing database (local dev, demo containers, the Northflank deployment) must be traded in once; the boot says how. `RETIRED_TABLES` in `db/bootstrap.ts` is append-only. Bumping the version remains a hand judgement in the same change as any non-additive edit to `schema.sql`.

### ADR-272 — the tournament is a package with two halves, and the dependency runs one way

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-270 (the removal this rebuilds on), `docs/design/tournament-engine.md` §1, the owner's tenet that the scheduler may lean on the tournament and never the reverse
- **Decision:** `packages/tournament` (`@psd/tournament`) holds the engine as pure TypeScript — no I/O, no clock, no randomness — in two halves: `src/core` (the tournament as data and decisions) and `src/scheduler` (format plugins, the planner, `simulate()`). The scheduler imports the core; the core never imports the scheduler; the package never imports the app or `@psd/contracts`. In the API the same split holds one layer out: `apps/api/src/tournament/` (core adapter) never imports `apps/api/src/tournament-scheduler/`, and only the route modules (the composition root) see both. A new `check-standards.mjs` rule, `tournament-direction`, fails the build on any import against the arrows.
- **Why:** The owner asked for a tournament "modularised and lightly coupled with the rest of the app", driven by a scheduler that can be switched off. A one-way dependency is what makes "switched off" mean something: with the scheduler terminated, the core still runs every match by hand because it never needed the scheduler. A pure package is also what lets the superadmin simulator run the very engine the day runs, in the browser. Rejected: one module with a `mode` flag — the coupling it hides is exactly what the reference implementations got wrong (their state machines lived inside the services).
- **Impact:** Root `typecheck` and `test` include the package; api and web resolve it through tsconfig `paths`; both Dockerfiles copy it. Engine refusal messages are developer fallbacks: the API maps refusal codes to `@psd/contracts` copy.

### ADR-273 — a seat names what fills it, and is frozen when someone sits in it

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** owner requirement 10, P-09, P-11; `packages/tournament/src/core/{types,seats,corrections,stages}.ts`
- **Decision:** Every match has two slots. A slot's source is a discriminated reference — `entrant`, `winner_of`, `loser_of`, `group_place`, `stage_place`, `pairing` (Swiss) or `vacant` — and the dependency edges between matches are exactly these references (a DAG, checked). Who would sit in a seat is derived on read (`resolveSource`); the seat is **frozen** into `seatedEntrantId` when its match starts or when a stage completion seats it, and a frozen seat never moves except by an attributable `reseat` with a reason. A correction (`correctResult`, walkover, void/unvoid) re-pays the match — voids its result awards and writes new ones — and reports every frozen dependent that would now read differently as a `seat_conflict` event for the desk; unfrozen dependents simply follow, because they were only ever forecasts.
- **Why:** Both reference implementations resolved seats lazily on every read and stored nothing at kick-off, so correcting a semi-final silently re-seated a final that had already been played. The problem catalogue's rule is "after people are sent somewhere, later corrections move tables, not people" — which needs the freeze. Rejected: rejecting corrections that touch dependents (Q1 left open by the catalogue, and a desk that cannot fix a typo is worse) and cascading them automatically (the reference failure).
- **Impact:** The database (ADR-275 onward) stores slots as rows with real foreign keys, not JSON.

### ADR-274 — formats are plugins that build a structure; one planner times every format

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** owner requirements 7–9, the owner's decision to support all nine reference formats plus open play; P-04, P-06, P-12, P-13
- **Decision:** A format is `{ validate, build(entrants, options) → Structure, restPolicy, isDynamic }`; the registry holds ten: open, round robin, groups → knockout, single elimination, double elimination (no reset), 8-team consolation (with 3rd and 5th place), Swiss (later rounds paired from standings with backtracking to avoid rematches; byes round the field), flighted quads, ironman (single elimination, zero rest, back-to-back flagged) and points rush (pools of three, group winners ranked overall). Byes are structure, never phantom matches; a third-place match exists only when two semi-final losers do; group play is interleaved by round. One planner (`plan`) places every format: list scheduling in priority order over the enabled courts, readiness from dependencies + changeover + rest + now, earliest-gap court choice with back-fill, live and pinned matches fixed, the next-up match per court kept in place across re-plans, unknown seats placed as forecasts. It returns placements and a fit summary (remaining matches, court-minutes, projected finish, deadline overrun) — advice, never a gate — and `diffPlacements` says what a re-plan would move.
- **Why:** The references ran each group to completion before the next (idling courts), treated cancelled matches as busy, ignored teams in live matches when re-planning and had one global court count. A single deterministic planner fed by the format's structure is what lets contingency (courts off, minutes changed) be previewed and applied, and lets the scheduler be switched off without losing the timetable.
- **Impact:** 68 engine tests (`packages/tournament/src/tests`), including per-format invariants: references always point at earlier matches, no vacant seats, double elimination plays 2n − 2 matches, Swiss never rematches when it can avoid it.

### ADR-275 — the rebuilt tournament's tables: core, scheduler and points bridge, with the arrows one way

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-272 (one-way modules), ADR-273 (seats), ADR-271 (stale databases are traded in), fds.md §2.5/§2.6 (re-implemented, not restored)
- **Decision:** `schema.sql` gains three blocks. **Core:** `tournament_court` (venue courts, 1–20), `tournament` (draft/live/closed, its win/draw/loss active-day points, a `revision`; at most one open, `ux_tournament_one_open`), `tournament_entrant` (the one seam to the app: `team_id → team`, name snapshot, entry order, withdrawal), `tournament_stage`, `tournament_group` + `tournament_group_entrant`, `tournament_match` (status, court, plan, score, result, void, `version`; one live match per court), `tournament_slot` (ADR-273's sources as real foreign keys, the frozen `seated_entrant_id`), `tournament_award` (append-and-void active-day points) and `tournament_event` (append-only history with actor snapshots). **Scheduler:** `tournament_scheduler` (format, options, timing, deadline, auto-advance, active/terminated) and `tournament_scheduler_pin`, both pointing at the core. **Points bridge (app side):** `tournament_match_roster` and `tournament_award_roster` freeze who on a team a match or award paid (ADR-005's grammar). Drizzle mirrors all of it in `db/schema/tournament.ts`.
- **Why:** The references kept match-to-match links in JSON with no integrity and no actor anywhere; the slot table makes every dependency a checked reference and the event table makes every decision attributable. Keeping the scheduler's tables pointing *into* the core is what lets the scheduler be terminated — or never created, for open play — without the core noticing. Reusing the names `tournament`, `tournament_match` and `tournament_stage` is safe because ADR-271 refuses any database built by the old snapshot; `RETIRED_TABLES` keeps only the names this schema does not define again.
- **Impact:** `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 2: no database was ever stamped 2 with the interim (tournament-less) snapshot outside this branch's own test runs. Actors are snapshots (kind, id, label), not foreign keys, so an account rename or retirement never rewrites the day's history.

### ADR-276 — the points bridge freezes who a tournament payment reached, at kick-off for a match and at the moment for an award

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** owner requirement 6 ("behind the scenes, the individual members will receive points"); ADR-005 (roster snapshots), ADR-006 (the board computed on read), ADR-248 (team awards on the same grammar), ADR-272 (the core knows no people), ADR-275 (the bridge's two tables)
- **Decision:** The engine pays entrants (`tournament_award`); the leaderboard pays people. `apps/api/src/routes-tournament/bridge.ts` joins them, app-side, inside the engine command's own transaction through a new `afterPersist` hook on `runCommand` (`runBridged`, used by every composition-root command): every match that just kicked off has both rosters frozen into `tournament_match_roster` — re-frozen if a match handed back to the queue kicks off again, since nothing was paid against the first — and every new award gets a `tournament_award_roster`: a result award copies its match's kick-off roster, so a correction that re-pays a match hours later pays the same people; a desk award, or a result with no kick-off (a walkover, a bye), takes the team as it stands. The scheduler's own payments (a Swiss bye) are frozen by `sweepRosters`, which `afterWrite` runs after every re-plan: the scheduler adapter cannot know the app's people, and the sweep is idempotent. The leaderboard's `tournament_points` arm is now team awards (ADR-248) **plus** non-voided tournament awards over their frozen rosters; `hasScoringStarted` counts a live tournament payment as scoring, so a cluster move after the first result is refused as it is after the first scan.
- **Why:** ADR-005 froze at completion; the rebuild freezes at kick-off, because that is when the engine freezes the seats — who played is who was on the team when it started, and a player who joins mid-match is not paid for a match they watched. Corrections and voids need no knowledge of rosters at all: the engine voids awards rather than editing them, and a re-payment copies the kick-off roster, so the board is always "non-voided awards × their frozen rosters". Rejected: writing rosters in the core adapter (it would import the app's people, against ADR-272) and computing rosters on read from live membership (the ADR-005 failure: a transfer would move historical points).
- **Impact:** Tests: `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-points-bridge.test.ts` (6, real PGlite, read off `/api/me/scans` and `/api/leaderboard`): kick-off freeze, the mid-match joiner unpaid, a correction re-paying the same people, void and unvoid, a desk award paying the current team and stopping on void, the cluster column. **Bite checks, each watched to fail:** an award roster taken from the live team instead of the kick-off (4 tests fail); the leaderboard arm without `voided_at IS NULL` (4 tests fail).

### ADR-277 — the rebuilt tournament is served at the old paths, in the old shapes, so the kept surfaces never change

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** fds.md F22–F25, S17, S21, S60; ADR-089 (schedule suggests, matches are the truth), ADR-091 (up soon), ADR-097 (recent teams), ADR-108 (one live match per team), ADR-109 (feed order), ADR-114/152 (the score is the result), ADR-131 (the frame is the response), ADR-150 (the bracket read), ADR-272 (composition root); the owner's rule that participant, facilitator and hall-screen code stays untouched
- **Decision:** `apps/api/src/routes-tournament/` serves every path the kept code calls — `GET /api/tournament/{courts, courts/:courtId/current-match, courts/:courtId/recent-teams, schedule, lineups, matches/feed, matches/:matchId, bracket}`, `POST /api/tournament/{matches, matches/:matchId/score, …/complete, …/cancel}` and `GET /api/teams/:teamId/matches` — in the wire types it already imports (`CourtView`, `MatchView`, `FixtureView`, `TournamentView`, `TournamentBracketView`, `UpSoonView`), filled from engine state by `views/tournament.ts`. The directory is the composition root: `support.ts` reads the day once (`readDay`, cached two seconds and voided by every tournament write), maps a staff session to the engine's actor, and runs what a write means for the app (`afterWrite`: void the day, the live feed, the board when a result moved, then `reconcile`); a point press voids the live picture only. The day a reader sees is the live tournament, else the one closed most recently (`findDayTournament`) — its results stand; a draft shows nobody anything. Two console acts gain engine commands, in `core/claims.ts`: **start** claims the queued structure match for the unordered pair (this court's first, then the earliest) and only otherwise stages an ad-hoc match, allowed while the scheduler runs by the owner's decision; **cancel** hands a claimed match back to the queue (`releaseMatch`: seats kept, score and start cleared — the matchup is still owed, ADR-089's release) and cancels an ad-hoc one outright. Engine refusal codes become HTTP statuses and `@psd/contracts` copy in one table (`refusals.ts`). The shared result rule (`lib/matchResult.ts`, ADR-157) is restored unchanged at the edge, because the wire's `null` winner is a **declared** draw the engine command cannot express. The §4.2.7 bootstrap gate reads "a tournament is live", since the rates now live on the tournament. The ADR-131 push pairs are restored in `check-standards.mjs` against the engine's command names (`startPair`, `scoreStep`, `completeMatch`, `callOff`, `correctResult`, `setMatchVoided` → `publishFeedMatch`; results also → `pushLeaderboard`).
- **Why:** The kept surfaces cannot move to meet the rebuild, so the contract is the paths and the shapes, byte for byte; a second set of paths would have been a second contract nobody calls. Claiming by pair (not by fixture id) is what the console already sends, and is why an overridden A/B order still fulfils the schedule. Handing a claimed match back rather than cancelling it is the old fixture release, said in the engine's terms: cancelling it would have dropped an owed group match from the day. Rejected: teaching the engine a "declared draw" — a draw on a non-level score is a desk correction, not a court act, and the edge rule already says so in the copy the marshal reads.
- **Impact:** `assignedFacilitatorId/Username` are null on every court (court assignment did not survive the removal; nothing on the kept surfaces writes it). A cancelled claimed match answers `status: 'cancelled'` on the wire while its row is `scheduled` again — the wire's word for "off this court", which is all the console and the feed read. Tests: `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-routes.test.ts` (12, real PGlite, including the wrong party on every console route), four authorization-matrix rows, `packages/tournament/src/tests/core-claims.test.ts` (7). **Bite checks, each watched to fail:** removing the edge result check (2 route tests fail: the contradicting winner and the declared draw on 1 − 0); making cancel always cancel (the hand-back test fails); dropping `publishFeedMatch` from the score handler (`push-pairing` fails `npm run standards`).

### ADR-278 — the scheduler adapter: a Swiss bye is a credited result, a person's move is a core command, and group-mates meet late

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-272 (one-way modules), ADR-273 (seats), ADR-274 (formats + planner), ADR-275 (tables); owner requirements 8 and 9; `apps/api/src/tournament-scheduler/{scheduler,materialise,planning,control}.ts`, `packages/tournament/src/core/{rounds,placement}.ts`. ADR-276 (points bridge) and ADR-277 (compatibility contract) stay reserved for the changes that ship them.
- **Decision:** The scheduler adapter is four files. `scheduler.ts` activates a format: it builds the structure over the non-withdrawn entrants in entry order, gives it ids (`materialise.ts`, which mints through `db/ids.ts` and rewrites every code reference), writes it with the core's `insertStructure`, writes the `tournament_scheduler` row (open play's is born `terminated`, because it has nothing to plan) and puts the tournament live — one transaction. `planning.ts` holds `reconcile(now)`: a no-op unless the scheduler is `active`; otherwise it closes every unambiguously finished stage as the seeded `system` actor (a tie on a cut line is refused by the core and left for a person), runs the Swiss step, then plans every scheduled match that is neither live nor pinned onto the enabled courts and writes the placements, returning `diffPlacements` against what was there. `control.ts` holds the contingency pair — `previewContingency` plans with the proposed courts and timings and writes nothing; `applyContingency` switches the courts, sets the timings, re-times every unplayed match of the tournament and reconciles — `terminate` (irreversible; placements stay where they were), and the pin: `moveMatch` makes the move with the core's new `placeMatch` command (attributable, an event) and, only while the scheduler runs, upserts a pin so the planner keeps it there; `releasePin` stamps `released_at` rather than deleting. Two engine additions: **byes as results** (`recordBye`) — a completed, one-seat `result_kind = 'bye'` match that pays the win rate and that every table, the rematch rule and "who has had a bye" read like any other result — and **`appendRound`**, the next Swiss round paired by the scheduler with its bye in the same decision. The Swiss step records the bye an odd field still owes (round one's, which a structure cannot hold) before pairing anything. And the groups → knockout seeding now deals each place's qualifiers to the free seed furthest from their own group-mates in the bracket, so a winner never meets its runner-up in the first round (1A v 2B, 1B v 2A) and two qualifiers of one group meet at the latest the bracket allows.
- **Why:** The engine already computed a Swiss bye (`planNextSwissRound().byeEntrantId`) and nothing recorded it, so an odd Swiss field quietly lost a team a round — the format's rule is "bye = walkover win", and a win that is not written down is not one. Writing it as a match row rather than a flag keeps one source for every table and one place points are paid. Making a person's move a core command, not a scheduler write, is what lets "terminated" mean full manual control: with the scheduler stopped the move still happens, is still attributed, and nothing overwrites it. The old seeding put both of a group's qualifiers on adjacent seeds (A1 and A2 in the same first-round match for a two-group day) — a rematch of a group game in round one.
- **Impact:** `tournament_scheduler_pin.released_at` is added (in the table and as an ADR-168 additive line, since the table first shipped without it). New event kinds `round_paired`, `bye_recorded`, `match_placed`. `runCommand` takes an optional `idCount` for a command that creates a round. Tests: `packages/tournament/src/tests/core-rounds-placement.test.ts` (8) and a cross-group seeding case in `formats.test.ts`; `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-scheduler.test.ts` (10, real PGlite). **Bite checks, each watched to fail:** dropping `reconcile`'s `status !== 'active'` guard (4 tests fail: terminate, open play, refusals, Swiss); removing the owed-bye step (the Swiss test fails); planning a preview over every court instead of the proposed ones (the preview test fails); the old adjacent qualifier seeding (`K1-1 1st in Group A v 2nd in Group A`).

### ADR-279 — the superadmin's tournament console is its own API, answering every write with the whole Control read

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** owner requirements 4–9 and the restructured Tournament tab (Control, Timetable, Simulator); ADR-272 (composition root), ADR-277 (kept surfaces), ADR-278 (scheduler adapter); fds.md §2.5 `#obj-court` (court number 1–5, widened here)
- **Decision:** `/api/admin/tournament` (superadmin only; one authorization-matrix row) serves the console. **Reads:** `GET /` (the Control read: courts, the desk's tournament — the open one, else the last closed — with entrants and their awarded points, stages with group and stage standings and their one-line explanations, every match with frozen-seat flags and pins, the scheduler row, and the planner's fit; plus the teams the setup form can enter), `GET /timetable` (one lane per court in planned order, the unplaced, the fit), `GET /events` (the latest 200 history lines). **Setup:** `POST /courts`, `PUT /courts/:id`, `PATCH /courts/:id/enabled`; `POST /` (a draft: name, its own win/draw/loss rates, teams in seed order, names snapshotted), `POST /discard` (a draft closed with a reason, never deleted), `POST /activate` (format, options, timing, optional deadline — ADR-278's `activate`). **Matches:** `POST /matches/:id/{result, walkover, void, reseat, cancel}` and `POST /matches` (staged by hand). **The day:** `POST /stages/:id/complete` (with overrides under one reason), `POST /entrants/:teamId/withdraw`, `POST /awards`, `POST /awards/:id/void`, `POST /contingency/{preview, apply}`, `POST /matches/:id/{move, release}`, `POST /scheduler/terminate`, `POST /close`. Every write is an engine command run as the superadmin or a scheduler-adapter call, goes through `afterWrite`, pushes what it changed (ADR-131 pairs extended to `stageAdHocMatch`, `recordWalkover`, `cancelMatch`, `awardPoints`, `voidAward`), and answers with the whole Control read. The contract lives in its own module, `packages/contracts/src/tournament.ts`. Court numbers run 1–20 (the table's CHECK since ADR-275), so `courtNumberInvalid` now says so — a recorded divergence from fds.md §2.5's 1–5. Withdrawing a team now also calls off the matches that name it outright before anyone is seated (a round robin's fixtures before kick-off), not only the ones whose seats were already frozen; a forecast seat ("Winner of #7") is left alone, because who fills it is undecided.
- **Why:** The desk decides with things no kept surface shows — frozen seats, pins, the explanation of a rank, the planner's fit — so it gets its own shapes rather than a stretch of the compatibility types. One read answering every write is what keeps a dense console honest: it never stitches a partial response onto a stale screen. The withdrawal gap was found by this suite: a round robin's matches are seated at kick-off, so the old rule ("a seat frozen to the team") cancelled nothing for a team that left before it played, and the planner kept placing a team that had gone home.
- **Impact:** Tests: `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-desk.test.ts` (13, real PGlite, reading every write back, plus the wrong party on the console); a new engine case in `core-corrections-stages.test.ts`. The Simulator subtab runs `simulate()` in the browser and has no endpoint. **Bite checks, each watched to fail:** withdrawal back to frozen seats only (the desk withdrawal test fails, and the new engine case did before the fix); `applyContingency` returning without writing (the contingency test fails).

### ADR-280 — the surfaces ADR-270 quietened read the rebuilt tournament again

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-270 (which returned neutral values from these readers until the rebuild), ADR-091 (up soon), ADR-151 (operations), ADR-154 (team repair), ADR-161 (final standings); fds.md §8.1 (the dashboard checklist)
- **Decision:** Every shared reader ADR-270 quietened reads the day again (`readDay`, the cached picture the kept surfaces share): the **dashboard** counts the venue's courts, enabled courts and the day's played matches (byes are not matches); **operations** lists live matches longest-first, each overdue against its own planned length, counts results inside the window, and reports the active teams that were not entered as `teamsOutside` with `canAdmit: false` — the rebuild has no late admission; **alerts** answer `teamUpSoon` with ADR-091's rule (the team's next unresolved match inside the first N line-up rows, N the enabled courts); the **repair console** names the court a team is playing on (`liveMatchCourtName`); a **court station** label is its `tournament_court` label again; **final standings** flatten the group tables (a team that had a walkover or bye is not fully scored, ADR-115) and read the podium off the bracket's final and third-place match, or — for a day with no final — off the last stage's table, withheld until every match is resolved. The repair console's `withdrawal` stays null: in the rebuild a team leaves a tournament only by the desk's explicit withdraw, never as a side effect of a roster fix.
- **Why:** ADR-270 kept these wires' shapes so the kept consoles would not change; this fills them from the engine rather than from the old fixture tables, through the same day picture the participant surfaces read, so the dashboard, the hall screen and the printed record cannot disagree about the day.
- **Impact:** Tests: `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-surfaces.test.ts` (5, real PGlite, a four-team single elimination with a third-place match). **Bite checks, each watched to fail:** an up-soon window that ignores the court count (the up-soon test fails); dropping the third-place place from the podium (the podium test fails).

### ADR-281 — what the tournament tables guarantee is constrained in the schema, and code reads it as guaranteed

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-013 (delete unreachable arms; never `v8 ignore`), ADR-080 (coverage ratchet), ADR-173 (a CHECK added as a named drop-then-add pair), ADR-275 (the tables), ADR-277 (the day a reader sees)
- **Decision:** Two more CHECKs on the rebuilt tables, each in the definition and as a named, re-runnable pair at the foot of `schema.sql`: `tournament_slot_pairing_check` (a pairing seat carries its stage, place and round, as the other source kinds already carry theirs) and `tournament_match_starter_check` (the starter snapshot is all three of kind, id and label, or none). Code that reads a value these constraints — or a foreign key, or the engine's own invariants — guarantee now uses `required(...)` instead of inventing a fallback (an empty id, an epoch timestamp, a missing slot read as "TBD"): slot sources in `load.ts`, the kick-off seats and entrant teams in the points bridge, fixed and finished placements in the planner, the day's start time and a court's recent teams in the reads, an accepted start's and stage's new match in the routes. The revision bump in `persist.ts` is `revision + 1` in SQL rather than read-then-write. `findDayTournament` no longer shows a discarded draft (closed without ever starting) as the day: it read to the room as a tournament already played.
- **Why:** ADR-080's floors found 270 uncovered branches in the new tournament code; most were fallbacks no input can reach, and ADR-013's method for those is deletion, not a test that manufactures an impossible database. Where the guarantee lived only in the code that writes the row, it now lives in the schema too, so `required` asserts a fact the database enforces rather than one it merely tends to hold.
- **Impact:** API coverage is back above every floor (branches 94.64% against 94.6%, functions 98.98% against 98.9%). New tests for the reachable edges: view edge cases and the shared result rule (`tournament-views.test.ts` 16), desk refusals and a discarded draft (`tournament-desk.test.ts` 16), console refusals, an idle venue and a closed day (`tournament-routes.test.ts` 16), a round-robin rostrum with a walkover and a court station's sign-in label (`tournament-surfaces.test.ts` 6), Swiss stopping after its last round (`tournament-scheduler.test.ts` 11).

### ADR-282 — two clocks for the tournament: the up-soon watcher returns, and the scheduler re-plans every minute

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-121 (the up-soon watcher, removed with the old tournament by ADR-270), ADR-082 (only `index.ts` starts a clock), ADR-274 (`reconcile`), owner requirement 8 (the timetable dynamically re-evaluated)
- **Decision:** `index.ts` starts two more intervals. The **up-soon watcher** (`lib/upSoonWatch.ts`, every 5 s) is ADR-121 restored over the rebuilt tournament: it reads the one cached day picture, answers every entered team with `upSoonOf`, and publishes a `team.upsoon` frame only for a team whose answer changed — into the window, nearer within it, or out of it — and skips the tick entirely while nobody is connected. The **scheduler tick** (`tickSchedule`, every 60 s) runs `afterWrite` with the clock: a running scheduler re-plans as time passes, not only when somebody writes, so a match running long pushes everything behind it before anyone asks. It never rejects — a failed re-plan is logged and the next tick tries again — and is a no-op without a running scheduler.
- **Why:** Writes already re-plan, but the plan also goes stale with nobody touching it: a quiet ten minutes on a court still moves every later start. The watcher exists for the reason ADR-121 gave — every write path moves the window, and instrumenting each is a promise the eleventh one breaks.
- **Impact:** Tests: `apps/api/src/tests/tournament-clocks.test.ts` (5): no frames to an empty room, two frames for the first pair then silence, a frame out of the window for the loser and in for the next pair, a later clock re-planning the queue, a failing database leaving the tick resolved. **Bite check watched to fail:** publishing every team's answer on every tick instead of only the changes (the "stays quiet" test fails).

### ADR-283 — a match with no planned time sorts after every one that has one, numerically

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-277 (line-up order), ADR-279 (the desk's lanes and queue)
- **Decision:** Every "planned start, then the structure's order" sort compares instants as numbers, with a missing time as `+∞` (`plannedMs` in `routes-tournament/support.ts`, its twin in the web's `useTournamentDesk`), never as strings with a placeholder.
- **Why:** The first versions sorted `plannedStartAt ?? '~'` with `localeCompare`, on the assumption that a tilde sorts after any ISO digit. It does not: locale collation puts `'~'` *before* `'2026-…'`, so a match the planner could not place led the participants' line-ups, the court console's offers and the desk's queue. The web hook's test caught it; the same sort was then found in two API files.
- **Impact:** A regression test pins the order (`tournament-views.test.ts`: live first, then by instant, then by sequence, the unplaced last), watched to fail against the tilde sort.

### ADR-284 — the court console gains a Line-ups subtab, as a new page beside the kept one

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** the owner's request for "a similar cut down interface on a subtab to show future line ups for his current assigned court"; the owner's rule that the facilitator frontend stays untouched; ADR-277 (`FixtureView`), ADR-283 (play order)
- **Decision:** `GET /api/tournament/courts/:courtId/lineups` (facilitator only; 404 for an unknown court; empty when no tournament is live) returns this court's unresolved matches in play order, in the kept `FixtureView` shape. The web page is `/staff/court/:courtId/lineups` — `apps/web/src/routes-court/CourtLineupsPage.tsx`, inside the kept `StaffShell`, with a two-link strip (Console, Line-ups). Each row reads "#seq team v team" (a seat not yet known reads "Winner of #7", "Loser of #7" for a third-place seat, or "To be decided"), with "On court now" for the live match, the planned start otherwise, and the first row marked "Up next on this court". It is a new directory rather than a change to `routes-facilitator/`, so the kept console is byte-for-byte unchanged; `check-standards.mjs`'s text-only rule (no avatars, no `gb-*`) now covers `routes-court/` too.
- **Why:** The marshal at a court needs the next pair and the one after, not the day: the Timetable is the desk's; this is its one-court cut. Putting it beside the kept page rather than inside it is what the owner's rule requires; the console page does not link to it yet, because adding the link would be editing the kept file — the subtab strip is on the new page, and the Stations list still opens the console.
- **Impact:** Tests: two route tests in `tournament-routes.test.ts` (this court only, in play order; the wrong party; an unknown court; a closed day) and `routes-court/CourtLineupsPage.test.tsx` (3). One authorization-matrix row widened. A link from the kept console to this subtab is the obvious next change once the owner lifts the freeze on facilitator files.

### ADR-285 — a facilitator's court station is picked from the venue's courts again

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** S45 (default station), ADR-270 (which left the court choice empty), ADR-280 (the court station's label restored on the API side)
- **Decision:** The facilitator form's station picker offers the venue's courts for a `court` station, read off the tournament console (`GET /api/admin/tournament` → `courts`), as it offers activities for a fringe station. The superadmin dashboard and operations panel needed no web change: they render fields the API now fills (ADR-280).
- **Why:** With courts back as `tournament_court` rows, an empty court list made it impossible to assign a marshal to a court from the console — the one surface that does it.
- **Impact:** `useAdminAccounts` reads two lists; its test pins both the court and the empty `none` case.

### ADR-286 — the demo day has its three courts and still no tournament

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-203 (the demo starts no tournament), ADR-264/270 (the regenerated seed), ADR-279 (courts are the desk's)
- **Decision:** `scripts/seed-demo.mjs` creates the venue's three courts through the desk API (`POST /api/admin/tournament/courts`, idempotent on a taken number) and still starts no tournament. `demo-export-cli.ts` exports `tournament_court`; every other tournament table is empty in the demo and stays unlisted, so a populated one still fails the export's coverage check. `seed-demo.sql` is regenerated from the recorded dump (`./refresh-demo-seed.sh --skip-record`, 120 participants verified).
- **Why:** ADR-203's demo is "after the briefing, before the first whistle: teams formed, the courts exist". Without courts the Simulator plans on none and Start has nowhere to put the day.
- **Impact:** A fresh demo shows Court 1–3 on the court picker, the Timetable's lanes and the Simulator's defaults.

### ADR-287 — navigations commit with the state change: sign-out lands on the front door

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-167 (a sign-out the server did not confirm has not happened), ADR-170/171 (the parallel browser suite), ADR-063/125 (the nav lights)
- **Context:** `e2e/acceptance/signout.spec.ts` had failed on every run since it was first executed, on the base commit of this sprint as well (`2bf76f4`, measured on a separate worktree and stack), and ADR-260's note recorded it as a known failure. The sign-out itself worked: `POST /api/auth/signout` answered 200 and the cookie was dead. The participant was then shown the sign-in form, not the front door the spec asks for. React Router 7 wraps every navigation in `React.startTransition` unless `useTransitions={false}`. `endSession` sets the session to `null` (an urgent update) and the profile page then navigates to `/` (a transition), so React renders the urgent update first, against `/me`: its `RequireActor` sees no session and redirects to `/signin`, and the transition to `/` is superseded. The jsdom acceptance test asserted the sign-in form, so it certified the defect instead of catching it.
- **Decision:** `apps/web/src/AppRouter.tsx` owns the router: `AppRouter` is `BrowserRouter useTransitions={false}` (used by `main.tsx`), and `TestRouter` is the matching `MemoryRouter` for a test that renders the whole app. `acceptance/signout.test.tsx` renders through `TestRouter` and asserts the landing page (`landing__signin`) and the absence of the sign-in form.
- **Also in this change (e2e isolation, no product code):** `e2e/participant/team-chat.spec.ts` asserted a bare `gameboy-shell__nav-alert`, which matched the Social light as well whenever another parallel file had just posted in the global room; it now asserts the Teams light by its label (`teamLight`). `team-chat-typing.spec.ts` signed up `unique('Watcher')`, the same label `chat.spec.ts` uses, so two files on one worker could collide on the nickname; it is `Lookout` now. `e2e/exclusive/service-worker.spec.ts` needs a built bundle (`dist/sw.js`), as its header says: run it with `npm run build:web`, the API serving `WEB_DIST`, `PSD_E2E_NO_SERVER=1` and `PSD_E2E_BASE_URL` (8 passed that way; against the Vite dev server it cannot pass).
- **Bite checks:** the jsdom test was changed first and watched failing (2 of 4: "Unable to find … landing__signin") before the router changed; `signout.spec.ts` then passed on both Chromium projects. The Teams-light locator, given a wrong label, failed `team-chat.spec.ts` at the "lights before they open it" step.
- **Impact:** No navigation in the app is deferred any more. Nothing in the app depended on the deferral: no `lazy` route, no `Suspense` boundary, no `useTransition`.

### ADR-289 — the desk puts a queued match on a court by hand, with no reason asked

- **Status:** Accepted

- **Context:** `POST /matches/:id/move` and `/release` existed (ADR-279) without a caller. Once the scheduler is stopped for good, nothing else on any surface could change where or when a queued match is planned — requirement 9 asks for full manual control.

A move is not a correction — it changes no result — so it does not go through the ReasonDialog (fds.md §2.13 governs results). With the scheduler running the move is pinned and the planner plans around it; once stopped, the move is simply where the match now is. The form follows the match: if a poll shows it has started meanwhile, the form closes.

### ADR-292 — `./verify.sh` runs the engine's own suite

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Relates to:** ADR-272 (`@psd/tournament`), ADR-080 (coverage ratchets), `AGENTS-workflow.md` §4
- **Context:** `npm test` (and so `npm run verify`) runs `test:tournament` first, but `./verify.sh` lists its stages by hand and had only `api tests` and `web tests`: the documented merge gate passed without running the engine's 85 tests or its coverage floor (lines/functions/statements 95, branches 90).
- **Decision:** a `tournament tests` stage before the API's. Measured at the change: 85 passed; statements 99.74%, branches 93.51%, functions 99.48%.

### ADR-269 — team chat gets the global room's polling fallback: transport parity between the two rooms

ADR-119's watchdog note recorded the asymmetry plainly: the global room had a fallback (`usePolling(room.isLive ? noop : room.catchUp)`, the jittered 45–75 s catch-up of ADR-024) and *"the team room has no poll at all — a dead stream there is simply a room that never updates again."* Reconnect-or-nothing was survivable while both rooms' streams were equally reliable, but it makes the team room strictly more fragile in exactly the environments the global room's fallback exists for: a browser with no `EventSource` (which gets the mount-time read and then silence for ever), or a socket wedged in a way the 70-second watchdog has yet to declare stale. The user asked for parity, and ADR-267/268's lesson is that the two rooms drift wherever they are allowed to differ. ADR-269 therefore gives the team room the global room's arrangement, unchanged in shape:

- `useTeamChatRoom` now ends its assembly with `usePolling(room.isLive ? noop : room.catchUp)` — the same line, the same jitter, the same suppression while live. The catch-up is the ADR-087 delta from the remembered tail's newest id, so a poll costs what the global room's costs: one cached delta read, merged idempotently; and per ADR-268's mirrored line it also reaffirms the read mark when the delta is empty.
- **What parity does not claim:** typing indicators stay stream-only (the poll carries messages, not keystrokes), the watchdog still owns stream *revival* (the poll catches the list up; it does not restore the live hint or the socket), and a healthy stream still suppresses the poll entirely — a wedged-but-open socket is caught by the watchdog's 70 s frame-silence rule (server heartbeats every 25 s; `STREAM_STALE_MS`), after which both transports are briefly active and the merge makes that harmless.
- The stale comments went with the change: `useTeamChatStream`'s revival note and `streamWatchdog.ts`'s header no longer describe a poll-less team room.

**Status:** Implemented (`useTeamChatRoom.ts`; comments in `streamWatchdog.ts`). Pinned in `TeamChatPanel.test.tsx`: with `EventSource` absent (the stream stub restored — jsdom's native state is the no-stream browser), the room shows the mount-time read, says live updates are off, and a message that only a poll can deliver appears after the jittered wait; the pre-existing stream-arrival and watchdog tests stand. `./verify.sh` fully green. Playwright was NOT run — the field check is a browser with the stream blocked or unavailable in team chat: the room should now refresh within ~75 s instead of never.

### ADR-268 — a caught-up room marks itself read: the global room gets the team room's empty-delta line

**Field report:** in the dev environment (status stream not arriving, so the alerts watermark moved only on the 45–75 s fallback poll), the Social tab's red LED could not be cleared by reading the global chat — opening the room, leaving, and returning any number of times changed nothing. The diagnosis is an asymmetry between the two rooms. `absorb` in both marks read only on a non-empty batch (ADR-083). The **team** room's catch-up therefore carries an extra line — *"a zero-message delta still means the remembered tail is visibly read now"* — firing `onRead` when the delta is empty but a remembered tail exists, and `TeamChatPanel.test.tsx` has pinned that behaviour since ADR-125. The **global** room's catch-up never got the line: open on the ADR-112 remembered tail, catch up with an empty delta, and the read mark simply never advances. Once the watermark sits ahead of the mark (one message arriving while the stream is down is enough — the poll moves the watermark, the room's cache absorbs the message on the next visit, and every visit after that is the same empty delta), the mark is frozen behind it permanently and the dot is mathematically unclearable by reading.

**Decision.** Mirror the team room exactly: `useChatRoom`'s catch-up now records `previousNewest` before the fetch and calls `onRead()` when the page is empty and a tail was held. Nothing else changes — an entirely empty room still reports nothing read (there is nothing to have read; that pin stands), the mark still advances only to the alerts store's held watermark, and the gallery's load-keyed marking is untouched. Two rooms with one read-marking rule each is the smell ADR-163's shared divider was created to avoid; this closes the hook-level instance of it by copying the proven implementation rather than inventing a second one.

**Status:** Implemented (`useChatRoom.ts`), with the regression pinned at hook level in `useChatRoom.test.ts` ("marks the room read on an empty delta, because the remembered tail is what was read" — verified to fail with the line removed) beside the team room's existing panel-level pin of the same behaviour; `./verify.sh` fully green. Playwright was NOT run (no browser in the sandbox). The handset/dev check is the report itself: with the status stream down, light the dot, read the room, leave, return — the LED now clears on the first visit.

### ADR-267 — the "new messages" line is drawn over the entry load, so your own message can never sit under it

ADR-163 froze the read mark at entry and held it for the visit, but computed the line's *placement* against the live list on every render. In a room the reader was fully caught up on, the first message newer than the frozen mark was therefore whatever arrived next — and the most reliable such message is the reader's own: type, send, and your line appeared under a fresh "new messages" separator, as reported from the handset. ADR-083 had already ruled the underlying principle ("absorbing is reading — nothing that lands in an open room is unread"); the divider simply had not been told. ADR-267 tells it, in shared machinery, so the global and team rooms cannot drift apart on this either:

- **A horizon joins the mark.** `useNewMessageBoundary` now also freezes the newest `createdAt` the entry load brought — the *horizon* — and only messages at or under it can sit below the line. The mark says where the reader stopped; the horizon says what "while you were away" consists of. Anything absorbed during the visit — the reader's own send above all, but equally a neighbour's live arrival — is past the horizon and draws no line and triggers no scroll-to-line. Earlier history loaded behind *Earlier messages* is under the horizon by construction, so the line can still climb to cover unread the opening page had not reached.
- **Settling is its own signal.** The horizon must not pin at the seeded cache's newest line (ADR-112), or it would fence out exactly the away-messages the catch-up delta is about to land. Both room hooks therefore expose `entrySettled`, false until the entry catch-up lands, which the panels pass to the boundary hook. This is deliberately a *new* fact rather than a redefinition of `isLoading`: ADR-112 pins "opens on the cached tail instantly, not-loading from the first paint" as a behaviour, and redefining the flag under it would have traded one ADR's contract for another's. A room that settles empty pins a null horizon — everything that ever arrives in it arrives in the reader's presence.
- **Nothing else about the line moves.** The mark is still a server timestamp, still frozen on first render, still string-compared; a message whose time equals the mark is still read; the scroll-to-line still happens once per visit, now only ever for a line present at settle.

**Status:** Implemented (`useNewMessageBoundary`, `useChatRoom`, `useTeamChatRoom`, `ChatPanel`, `TeamChatPanel`). Pinned at the hook (`useNewMessageBoundary.test.ts`: no line above a post-entry arrival, the found line holds under arrivals, the line climbs over loaded-earlier unread, the horizon waits for settle, an empty-settled room stays line-free) and end-to-end in `ChatPanel.test.tsx` (a caught-up reader sends; their line renders with no divider); `./verify.sh` fully green. Playwright was NOT run (no browser in the sandbox) — the handset check is the reported flow itself: send in global chat and see your message land as a message, not as news.

### ADR-266 — the QR badge shows its three essentials at full size and lets the rest scroll

ADR-098's shell never scrolls its frame, and the QR badge (S3) took the further step of never scrolling *itself*: a `useFitScale` hook measured the whole card against `.gb-main` and transform-shrank it (to no less than 0.7×) until nickname, QR code, spoken number, points total, profile link and decorative sand strip all fit the viewport at once. The field report inverts the priority: on the one screen a participant holds up at every fringe station, only **the participant's name, the QR code and the facilitator number** need to be seen — and the fit-to-viewport shrink made the QR code, the single element that must be scanned across a counter in glare, smaller to protect a points line and a row of crabs. ADR-266 therefore:

- **Removes the shrink.** `QrHomePage` no longer calls `useFitScale`; the hook and its test are deleted rather than left as dead machinery (the badge was its only caller). The card lays out at natural size in essentials-first order — nickname, code, spoken number — and on a short phone the points, the "My points" link and the sand strip fall below the fold inside `.gb-main`, which is what that scrolling region is for. ADR-098's shell model (frame is the viewport, `.gb-main` scrolls, nav cannot leave the screen) is untouched; only the badge's fit-the-whole-card gloss on it is superseded.
- **Spends the freed width on the code.** `.gb-qr` grows from `min(260px, 70vw)` to `min(320px, 76vw)` — as wide as the padded column allows, since scan distance and glare, not card elegance, set the requirement. The spoken number keeps ADR-103's gold pill; nothing about the scan contract changes, and all testids (`qr-home__fallback`, `qr-home__scan-number`, `qr-home__profile`) stand.

**Status:** *(ADR-318 refines this: the code now also shrinks to the height left, so the spoken number stays above the fold.)* Implemented (`QrHomePage.tsx`, `styles/gameboy.css`); pinned in `styles/gameboy.css.test.ts`; `./verify.sh` fully green. Playwright was NOT run (no browser in the sandbox) — the handset check is that name, code and number are all visible without scrolling on the reporting phone and the code scans at counter distance, with the points line a short scroll below.

### ADR-265 — the participant theme is sized and backed for the phone it actually runs on

The participant surfaces are a phone app that was styled on a desktop monitor. Three reports from the reporting Android handset, all on the root page: the UI opened looking **very zoomed out**; pinch-zooming toward the heading and the panel left **only flat sky** behind them, the backdrop nowhere in sight. Nothing was broken in the browser-zoom sense — the viewport meta has been correct since the first commit (`width=device-width, initial-scale=1`) — the page *read* as zoomed out because the pixel type is sized for across a desk (Press Start 2P at 8–15 px, a 20 px reading face), and the backdrop read as absent because of the geometry ADR-256 chose. ADR-265 fixes the sizing and the sky, and re-examines — and keeps — ADR-256's bargain:
